content.text:
I fixed it in `src/rules_inline/backticks.ts`. Now `[foo `bar` baz``, `![alt `code` x`` and `[`a`b`` render the code span the way the CommonMark reference does. The code is identical to upstream 15.0.0, so the bug is there too.

**Cause:** the backtick rule keeps a cache of where it last saw a run of N backticks. Once a scan reaches the end of the line, any opener with no cached run after it is treated as having no closer, and is output as literal text. There were two problems with how that cache was filled:
1. When a code span matched, the closing run's position was never cached.
2. A later scan that started earlier on the line could overwrite an entry with a smaller position.

An unclosed `[` / `![` triggers this because the link rule first looks ahead through the label in silent mode. In `[`a`b``, that look-ahead matches `` `a` ``, then scans from the last backtick to the end of the line. When the real parsing pass reaches the backtick at position 1, the cache wrongly says no closer exists.

**Fix:** every backtick run found during a scan, including a matched closer, is now recorded in the cache, and an entry is only ever moved to a later position. That makes "nothing cached after this opener" mean there really is no closer.

**Tests:** I added four regression cases to `test/fixtures/markdown-it/commonmark_extras.txt`: the link and image cases from the report, the minimal trigger, and a case mixing code spans of different lengths. The full `test/markdown-it` suite passes (299/299), and the CommonMark spec tests showed no failures in their dot output.

- **Fixtures against the old code:** I couldn't confirm the new cases fail before the fix. The stash command didn't run, so nothing in your working tree was touched.
- **eslint:** lint wasn't run on the changed file.
